content_sections.title: Learn the management sense of run
content_sections.body_text: Here run means manage or organize an activity, service, or organization. ‘Lan runs a language club.’ ‘They run a weekend course.’ Identify what is managed after run, then create one true or invented example about a club, event, service, course, or business.

content_sections.title: Place management before a past point
content_sections.body_text: Guests arrived for the club meeting at 6:00 Friday. Earlier, Lan had run three school events. Had run puts her organizing experience before that clear anchor. Draw HAD RUN EVENTS → GUESTS ARRIVED, 6:00 FRIDAY → now; keep the management meaning.

content_sections.title: Mark linking boundaries
content_sections.body_text: Many accents can join a final consonant smoothly to a following vowel: run_an event; event_at school. Practise each side, then the pair with no added pause or vowel. Keep /n/ and /t/ audible. Timing varies by accent; aim for clear words, not one accent.

content_sections.title: Notice, retell, self-check
content_sections.body_text: Model: ‘At 6:00 Friday, guests arrived. Earlier that day, Lan had run_an event_at school, so she knew how to organize the club.’ Mark the past anchor, rehearse both possible links, then retell with another activity. Check: run means manage, had run is earlier than 6:00, and your accent keeps every word clear.
